description: Put the pointer on an element AND LEAVE IT THERE, then report what that revealed: a menu that opens on hover, a tooltip, the actions a row only shows under the pointer, the value a chart reads out beneath it. qa_click cannot answer any of those — it presses a millisecond after it hovers, and the press closes what the hover opened. It holds for `holdMs` (500 by default) before measuring, because tooltips wait — measuring at once reports "no tooltip" about one that was always going to appear. The reply carries the usual `changed` diff plus `tooltip` (role=tooltip, aria-describedby or title, whichever exists) and `expanded` when the control changed its aria-expanded. ONE FACT TO READ CAREFULLY: `cssHover` says whether the browser's own `:hover` matched. Dispatched events run the page's JavaScript handlers — every menu and tooltip library — but they do not move the real cursor, so an effect written PURELY in CSS does not appear and `cssHover` comes back false. That is the tool being honest, not the page being broken. With trusted input switched on the real pointer moves, `cssHover` is true, and CSS-only hovers light up too. Call it again with `off: true` to take the pointer away — "the tooltip disappears" is the other half of the check, and it needs its own call. Requires the one-time “Agent control” confirmation in the panel; without it the extension answers consent-required and does nothing.

holdMs.description: How long to hold the pointer there before measuring (0–10000, default 500)

off.description: Take the pointer AWAY from whatever it is on, and report what was left. No target needed.

ref.description: A ref from qa_snapshot (e.g. "e12") — preferred over selector

selector.description: CSS selector of the element to hover

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

x.description: Without ref/selector: CSS pixels from the LEFT of the viewport. WITH one: an offset inside the element, for a chart or a split control where the middle is the wrong place.

y.description: Without ref/selector: CSS pixels from the TOP of the viewport. WITH one: an offset inside the element.

name: qa_hover
title: Hover over an element and hold
